name: Global AI
desc: Designs, builds and operates single-tenant, air-gapped AI data centres running Nvidia systems for nations and organisations.
markets: Operates a GPU data centre in Endicott, New York; plans further US capacity; customer names not disclosed; no verified sites abroad.
rationale: B2B infrastructure firm selling to governments and large organisations; F1 hospitality could help win clients, but brand reach is limited.
changed: Partnership with HUMAIN (PIF company) to build US AI capacity announced in December 2025

name: Horizon3.ai
desc: Sells NodeZero, an autonomous penetration testing platform that finds and exploits network weaknesses for enterprises and governments.
markets: US headquarters; EMEA headquarters opened in Amsterdam in 2026; ASEAN hub planned in Singapore; staff in Australia.
rationale: Fast-growing cybersecurity vendor expanding into Europe and Asia-Pacific; rivals CrowdStrike and Zscaler use F1 for enterprise hospitality and brand.

name: Keel Infrastructure Corp.
desc: Develops and owns power-secured data centre campuses for AI and high-performance computing tenants in the United States and Canada.
markets: Site pipeline in Pennsylvania and Washington (US) and Québec (Canada); first HPC sites and revenues targeted for 2027.
rationale: Listed infrastructure developer courting hyperscaler tenants; little consumer brand need, so F1 value is limited to B2B hospitality.
changed: Renamed from Bitfarms Ltd. and redomiciled from Canada to the US on 1 April 2026

name: Vena Solutions
desc: Provides Excel-based cloud software for corporate budgeting, planning, forecasting and financial consolidation to mid-sized and large companies.
markets: Offices in Toronto, London and Indore, India, plus staff across the US and EU; customers mainly North America and Europe.
rationale: Mid-market B2B software vendor; F1 hospitality could target CFOs, but rivals' F1 presence is limited and brand budget modest.

name: CoinDCX
desc: Runs a cryptocurrency exchange app and website where retail users buy, sell and trade crypto, futures and staking products.
markets: Main market India; owns BitOasis in the UAE since 2024; launched in Bahrain; targeting wider GCC growth.
rationale: Consumer crypto brand growing in India and the Gulf; rivals Crypto.com, OKX and Kraken already sponsor F1, aiding Gulf race visibility.
changed: Acquired Dubai-based BitOasis in 2024; Coinbase investment announced, subject to regulatory approval

name: Inflection AI
desc: Develops enterprise AI systems that companies can own and customise, after building the Pi personal chatbot for consumers.
markets: US base; set up a London subsidiary in 2026 to re-establish UK presence; enterprise customers not disclosed.
rationale: Small enterprise AI vendor after losing most staff; F1 could showcase technology, but resources and brand reach look limited.
changed: Co-founder Suleyman and most staff joined Microsoft in 2024; refocused on enterprise AI

name: Alarm.com Holdings
desc: Provides cloud software for connected home and business security, video, energy and access control, sold through security dealers.
markets: Mainly US and Canada; international deployments through service-provider partners, reportedly including Latin America and Europe.
rationale: Listed B2B2C platform with dealer network; F1 hospitality could reward partners, though markets are mostly North American.

name: Verbit
desc: Provides AI and human-edited captions, transcripts and audio description for education, media, legal, government and corporate clients.
markets: Offices in the US, Canada, UK and Israel; freelance transcriber network across many countries; customers mainly North America.
rationale: B2B services firm with media clients; F1 broadcast captioning could be a showcase, but marketing budgets look modest.

name: Magic
desc: Develops AI models with very long context windows to help software engineers write and review code, offered to enterprises.
markets: Research-focused San Francisco team with roots in Vienna; no public self-serve product; no verified customers or international operations.
rationale: Research-stage AI lab with no public product or consumer brand; little reason to buy F1 visibility now; weak fit.

name: Mercor
desc: Recruits and manages networks of domain experts who train and evaluate AI models for leading AI labs.
industry: AI training data and expert marketplace
markets: Offices in San Francisco, New York and London; customers are mainly US AI labs such as OpenAI and Anthropic.
rationale: Fast-growing AI data firm whose clients include Anthropic, an F1 partner; F1 could build employer brand and expert recruitment globally.

name: Unconventional AI
desc: Early-stage AI hardware company developing new, more energy-efficient computing foundations for AI data centres.
markets: Pre-revenue; California-based team (headquarters city reported inconsistently); no verified customers or international operations.
rationale: Pre-revenue deep-tech hardware start-up with no product or customers to market; weak F1 fit for now.

name: Wrtn Technologies
desc: Operates the Wrtn generative AI app and story-driven AI character services Crack and Kyarapu for consumers.
markets: Users mainly in South Korea and Japan (Kyarapu, Japanese subsidiary); plans to enter the US market reported in 2026.
rationale: Consumer AI brand growing in Korea and Japan; F1 Japanese Grand Prix could support awareness, though fit is unproven.

name: Verda
desc: Rents GPU clusters and serverless AI inference from renewable-powered data centres to AI start-ups and enterprises.
markets: Data centres in Finland and Iceland; offices in Helsinki, London, Taipei and San Francisco; customers in over 50 countries.
rationale: European AI cloud challenger expanding into the US and Asia; F1 could showcase its compute and attract enterprise customers.

name: CADDi
desc: Provides CADDi Drawer, an AI drawing and manufacturing data platform, and sources made-to-order parts for manufacturers.
markets: Offices in Japan, the US, Vietnam and Thailand; supplier operations in Mexico; customers in 22 countries.
rationale: B2B manufacturing software with Japanese industrial clients; F1 engineering tie-in plausible, but brand marketing need is modest.

name: Hightouch
desc: Sells data activation software that syncs company data warehouses with marketing tools and runs AI marketing agents.
markets: Offices in San Francisco, New York and London (Sydney also reported); serves EMEA customers alongside its US base.
rationale: Marketing technology vendor whose clients include F1 partner WHOOP; F1 hospitality could reach brand CMOs, but scale is modest.

name: Profound
desc: Provides an AI visibility platform showing enterprise brands and agencies how they appear in chatbot answers.
markets: Offices in New York, San Francisco, London and Buenos Aires; Singapore office reportedly planned; enterprise customers mainly US.
rationale: Sells to brand marketers, the core F1 sponsor audience; F1 hospitality could reach CMOs, though the company is young.

name: Firebird
desc: Builds and operates Nvidia-powered AI cloud and supercomputing infrastructure in Armenia, renting compute to AI companies such as Perplexity.
markets: Offices in San Francisco and Yerevan; AI data centre in Hrazdan, Armenia, developed with the Armenian government; US customers.
rationale: Young B2B compute provider tied to one Armenian project; limited brand need, so F1 fit rests on client hospitality only.

name: Quantifind
desc: Provides AI software that screens entities for financial crime, money laundering and sanctions risk for banks and government agencies.
markets: Offices in Palo Alto, New York, Boston and Washington DC; Sydney office opened in 2026 to expand in Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Niche compliance software for banks; F1 hospitality could reach bank buyers, but brand marketing need is low.

name: Simile
desc: Sells AI agentic twins that simulate human behaviour so large companies can test decisions before real-world rollout.
markets: Customers include Fortune 100 enterprises; small team originating in Palo Alto; no verified international offices or expansion plans.
rationale: Young B2B AI firm selling market-research simulations; limited brand budget and no obvious F1 tie-in; weak fit.

name: Walden Robotics
desc: Builds wheeled, two-armed semi-humanoid robots for manufacturing and logistics work, offered to businesses as robots-as-a-service.
markets: Robots working at a Toyota facility in North America since 2026; other industrial customers unnamed; no verified international operations.
rationale: Toyota-backed robotics start-up; F1 engineering showcase is conceivable, but it is early-stage with little marketing need.
changed: Spun out of Toyota Research Institute in January 2026

name: Xoople
desc: Turns satellite imagery into AI-ready Earth data for governments and companies while developing its own satellite constellation.
markets: Platform in private preview with government and Fortune 500 users; staff in eight countries, mostly Spain; constellation not yet launched.
rationale: Pre-launch space-data firm with B2B and government buyers; little brand need, so F1 makes little commercial sense now.

name: Augustus
desc: Runs Augustus Bank, an OCC-chartered clearing bank offering real-time stablecoin and dollar settlement through its AI core banking platform.
markets: US federally chartered bank; customers include Kraken; plans to use 2026 funding to expand internationally.
rationale: Early-stage B2B clearing bank; F1 crypto and fintech sponsors are potential clients, but brand marketing need is low.
changed: Received OCC national bank charter for Augustus Bank, N.A.

name: Axiom Math
desc: Develops AI systems that generate verified mathematical proofs, with planned applications in software and code verification.
markets: Pre-revenue research company in Palo Alto; no verified customers or international operations.
rationale: Research-stage AI lab with no product or customers to promote; weak F1 fit.

name: XBOW
desc: Sells an autonomous AI penetration testing platform that continuously finds and validates security vulnerabilities for enterprises.
markets: Over 100 customers including Fortune 500 companies; sold via AWS Marketplace; no verified offices or customer breakdown outside the US.
rationale: Fast-growing cybersecurity vendor; rivals CrowdStrike and Zscaler use F1 for enterprise hospitality, giving a plausible tech-showcase fit.
